title: drMAIC 0.1.0 returns the MAIC estimate as its doubly robust estimate, with an interval six times too narrow
question: Does drMAIC 0.1.0 implement a doubly robust MAIC with valid intervals: is its augmented estimate robust to a wrong weighting model when the outcome model is right, and do its intervals cover?
design: Unanchored binary-outcome transport in a 2 x 2 of correct or wrong weighting and outcome models at two overlap levels; drMAIC's MAIC, DR estimate, analytic interval and bootstrap interval against a correctly augmented estimator. 8 cells, 600 replicates each, plus a bootstrap arm.
answer: No. drMAIC 0.1.0 averages the outcome model over the individual-data patients instead of the target population, so its doubly robust estimate equals its MAIC estimate in every replicate (difference below 2e-15) and keeps MAIC's bias when the weights are wrong and the outcome model right (0.066 against 0.004 for correct augmentation). Its analytic SE divides by n twice and mixes probability and log odds scales: 0.028 against an empirical SD of 0.17 to 0.22, coverage 0.20 to 0.26. Its percentile bootstrap covers 0.78 to 0.79.
findings: Defect 1: theta_stc = sum(w_norm * m_hat), so the augmented estimate reduces algebraically to the weighted mean of Y.
Defect 2 and 3: .dr_variance returns sum((w_norm*(Y-theta))^2)/n on the probability scale and it is reported as the SE of a log odds ratio.
Defect 4: bootstrap_ci() reweights on means only, refits the default outcome formula and holds the comparator fixed.
Wrong weights, right outcome model, target mean 0.5: drMAIC DR bias 0.066 (MCSE 0.007); correct augmentation 0.004; correct augmentation coverage 0.93 to 0.96 across cells.
not_answered: One package version, binary outcome, one sample size; G-MAIC not run; the time-to-event path (a weighted median labeled a hazard ratio) read from code, not simulated. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target-population marginal log odds ratio, A versus B
methods_compared: drMAIC doubly robust with analytic interval
correctly augmented weighting with bootstrap SE
n_sim: 600 per cell, 8 cells; package bootstrap 150 per cell in 2 cells
